LESSON: FABRIC DECORATION: BATIK.

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: FINE ARTS
Strand: Multimedia Arts (2D Art)
Topic 2.4: Fabric Decoration: Batik.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fabric Decoration: Batik., part of Multimedia Arts (2D Art) in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 FINE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is it not possible to have definite shapes when tie and dyeing? 2. What visual effect is observed in a fabric made using batik technique?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use digital devices to search information on batik focusing on; concept (Indonesia/ Ghana/Nigeria/Senegal), techniques (crackled effect, textured effect) and materials and tools, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use digital devices to search information on batik focusing on; concept (Indonesia/ Ghana/Nigeria/Senegal), techniques (crackled effect, textured effect) and materials and tools, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fabric Decoration: Batik. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: as the learner interacts with digital devices to search information on characteristics of fabrics

decorated by batik, tie and dye techniques

● Collaboration: as the learner actively collaborates in sourcing and cleaning used cotton fabrics

● Learning to learn: as the learner use digital devices to search information on batik
